drhp.business: UCAL designs, develops and manufactures Fuel Management Systems and mechatronic automotive components, spanning powertrain products (oil/vacuum/coolant pumps, VVT systems, water outlets, thermostats), air & fuel systems and emission controls (carburettors, throttle bodies, fuel rail assemblies, fuel injection parts), automotive electronics (sensors, ECUs, controllers, TPMS, ADAS-related sensing) and manufacturing services (pressure die casting and precision machined components, build-to-print products). Its products serve automotive OEMs, the aftermarket and non-automotive industries worldwide.

drhp.expansion: During the year UCAL commissioned new production lines for Mechanical Throttle Bodies, Crankcase and E-Purge Systems across its Bawal and Maraimalai Nagar (MM-1, MM-2) facilities. The Bawal plant achieved production ramp-up of two-wheeler and three-wheeler crankcase lines, including zero-defect manufacturing for the three-wheeler programme, and established automated throttle body lines for global OEM requirements. New manufacturing lines were also established: a Throttle Body line at the MM-2 Plant for two-wheelers/scooters, a Throttle Body line at Bawal with robotisation and AI-based quality controls for the two-wheeler/motorcycle aftermarket, a water-outlet line for 13 different models for Heavy Vehicles for the global aftermarket, an E-Purge Manufacturing Line at MM-1 Plant, and Crankcase manufacturing lines for 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers at Bawal for the export aftermarket. The Company further strengthened smart manufacturing with robotization, AI-based calibration verification and memory-lock systems with end-to-end traceability.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Throttle body and fuel rail assembly demand is expected to stay supported by hybrid applications, aftermarket requirements and cost-sensitive markets as the market gradually transitions to electronically controlled powertrains.
- Automotive pumps and valves demand is expected to benefit from the coexistence of ICE, hybrid and electric vehicles, each requiring increasingly sophisticated fluid management systems.
- VVT market outlook is favourable as hybrid vehicle production accelerates and regulatory standards tighten, with growth driven by electronically controlled valve technologies and hybrid architecture integration.
- ECU market is expected to see sustained growth driven by ADAS proliferation, connected vehicle technologies, electrification, software integration and consolidation of vehicle architectures into domain/zonal controllers.
- Automotive electronics market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 8% to 10%, driven by higher electronic intensity per vehicle and proliferation of software-defined vehicle architectures.
- Emission control systems demand is sustained by continued ICE production in emerging economies and expansion of hybrid powertrains; the global market is projected by IMARC Group to reach USD 40.57 billion by 2033 at a 6.11% CAGR (2025-2033).
- Die casting and precision machining outlook remains positive on demand across ICE, hybrid and EV platforms for lightweight structural components, battery housings/enclosures, transmission systems and e-axle components.
- Carburettor market is in long-term structural decline as EFI penetration deepens, with demand increasingly concentrated in legacy fleets, aftermarket replacement and price-sensitive micro-markets; UCAL's focus is on serving residual demand and aftermarket efficiently.
- Two-wheeler segment is a key growth driver for fuel injection systems globally, led by the transition from carburettor-based systems to EFI under emission norms such as BS-VI/Euro 5 equivalents, concentrated in Asia, Africa and Latin America.
- Overall sales grew 19% over the previous year despite the de-phasing of legacy e-Carb and EASV products; new products grew 150%, Aftermarket grew 32%, and OES (Spares) and OE grew 21% and 19% respectively.
- India's transition to green mobility, supported by government programmes such as the PM e-Drive Scheme and PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme and budget impetus for electronics and battery manufacturing, is a stated demand driver for UCAL's expanded EV product portfolio.
- A strong order pipeline in new products augurs well for FY 2026-27.
- A diversified mix of new products is in the pipeline in different stages of development and market launch.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: During the year UCAL commissioned new production lines for Mechanical Throttle Bodies, Crankcase and E-Purge Systems across its Bawal and Maraimalai Nagar (MM-1, MM-2) facilities. The Bawal plant achieved production ramp-up of two-wheeler and three-wheeler crankcase lines, including zero-defect manufacturing for the three-wheeler programme, and established automated throttle body lines for global OEM requirements. New manufacturing lines were also established: a Throttle Body line at the MM-2 Plant for two-wheelers/scooters, a Throttle Body line at Bawal with robotisation and AI-based quality controls for the two-wheeler/motorcycle aftermarket, a water-outlet line for 13 different models for Heavy Vehicles for the global aftermarket, an E-Purge Manufacturing Line at MM-1 Plant, and Crankcase manufacturing lines for 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers at Bawal for the export aftermarket. The Company further strengthened smart manufacturing with robotization, AI-based calibration verification and memory-lock systems with end-to-end traceability.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- integration: backward-integrated manufacturing across casting and precision machining facilities in its India plants — evidence: the AR states UCAL's backward-integration capabilities in casting and precision machining facilities across its Plants in India enable design and manufacture of High Pressure Die Casting and Precision Machined Products for mission-critical applications
- technology: dedicated, accredited in-house R&D infrastructure supporting mechatronic and electronics product development — evidence: an integrated DSIR-recognised and NABL-accredited R&D Centre and testing laboratory, together with a dedicated Electronics R&D

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The AR states the global carburettor market is in long-term structural contraction as EFI and electrified powertrains displace carburettors in developed markets, with demand concentrating in legacy fleets and price-sensitive niche segments; UCAL continues to de-phase its legacy e-Carb products.
- MD&A notes that while deemed exports saw significant demand, direct exports faced headwinds from tariff wars and geopolitical tensions during the year.
- Multiple product-line outlooks (throttle bodies, pumps & valves, VVT) describe a gradual transition away from purely mechanical, ICE-dependent technologies toward electronically controlled and hybrid/EV-aligned systems, requiring continued R&D investment to stay relevant.
- The Company manages risk 'by ensuring that customers underwrite the capacities created specifically for their requirements,' implying capacity is built against customer-specific programmes, a structural dependency on those customer commitments.
- The Board's risk framework explicitly classifies risks into financial, operational, market and statutory compliance categories, evaluated by probability of occurrence and business impact as part of the annual business plan.
- Management states it manages risk 'by localization to protect itself from exchange risks,' indicating foreign-exchange exposure tied to its export/global-sourcing business.
- The Board-level committee 'assists the management in assessing the market risks, competitors risks, product obsolescence risk and devises strategies to overcome the same.'

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Two-track growth strategy: strengthen the core (carburettors, fuel management systems, oil pumps, vacuum pumps) through deeper customer engagement, operational excellence and cost competitiveness, while building future-ready capabilities in sensors, actuators, controllers, electric pumps and intelligent electronic systems.
- Move up the value chain: progressively evolve from mechanical component manufacturing towards mechatronic products, modules, subsystems and complete system solutions, using own engineering strengths plus technology partnerships, collaborations and licensing arrangements where required.
- Expand beyond automotive: pursue adjacent industries where UCAL has 'a clear right to win' — the Company has already initiated expansion into defence and aerospace, and will selectively pursue generator and off-road equipment, followed by marine, industrial and energy applications.
- Build the UCAL Industrial Alliance: a structured ecosystem of trusted manufacturing partners whose products are brought to market under the UCAL brand, to expand the aftermarket portfolio faster while UCAL stays focused on its core manufacturing strengths.
- Global expansion: expand presence in Europe and North America, offering both products and manufacturing/engineering expertise, aiming to become a preferred global manufacturing partner.
- Expand automation and robotisation of processes across manufacturing plants to further strengthen future-ready manufacturing capabilities (stated Outlook priority).
